tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on the Harborview demo — outlined-text firms return zero room labels. v2 = productize the M3 tiles lane (opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action) + callout-vs-room filtering.

prep.what: Build the opt-in AI label-detection action for firms where PDFTron outlines all text (so the free lane finds nothing), and filter out non-room callouts like stair arrows and FEC notes.
prep.understand: The live-text lane works great when PDF text is readable (Holabird: 92/109 named). But firms that outline text return ZERO labels — PDFTron strips them all. The M3 tiles approach sends small page tiles to MiniMax image-01 (~4.3 min/sheet, costs credits via §7a metered event) and reads labels from pixels instead. Separately, callout noise is documented R13 polish: general-note paragraphs, 'UP' stair arrows, FEC callouts all match as room names and need to be filtered.
approach: Productize `run_labels_m3tiles.py` into a proper service route (e.g. POST `/sheets/{id}/actions/read-labels-ai`) behind a feature gate and the §7a metered-credits event — triggered by an 'Read labels (AI)' button, not auto-run.

Wire the MINIMAX_AI key to the VPS (make the secrets decision: env var in `.env` on `/opt/takeoff-engine`, same pattern as the existing API_KEYS_RAW). Until done, the route returns 503 with a clear message.

Implement the callout-vs-room filter: build a regex/rule set for Holabird's documented noise patterns (general-note paragraphs, `UP`/`DN` stair text, FEC/AED/EXIT callouts) and apply it as a post-processing step in the text-label lane.
Test on Harborview (the zero-label case) and re-run Holabird to verify the noise filter doesn't drop real room names.

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: PRD Phase 1. assemblies-lite scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py as of B1. Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar between us and estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Extend `engine/assemblies.py` from the scaffolded lite version to a full room-type → quantities engine: floor SF, wall SF, ceiling SF, base LF, paint SF — driven by room classification and wall heights.
prep.understand: The lite version is already wired into `build_sheet_takeoff` (the single orchestrator) and flows into the 5-tab Excel via `engine/excel.py`. Wall heights are already stored per-room via PATCH `wall_height_ft`. Room classifications are already produced by the engine. Your job is to fill in the *formula logic*: room_type + area + perimeter + height → up to 8 CSI-aligned quantities. This goes directly into the existing export pipeline — no new routes needed, just richer output from `assemblies.py`.
approach: Open `engine/assemblies.py` and understand the existing lite scaffold — what's already wired vs what's stubbed. Then open `engine/excel.py` to see how the assembly output maps to Excel tabs.

Define a room_type → assembly recipe table (e.g. Office: floor=area, ceiling=area, wall=perimeter×height, base=perimeter, paint=wall+ceiling; Bathroom: add waterproofing). Start with 4–5 types covering the bulk of CT Pros sheets.

Implement the quantity formulas: SF floor = polygon area (already in engine); SF wall = perimeter × wall_height (use stored height or default 9ft); SF ceiling = area; LF base = perimeter. For rooms with a missing wall_height, emit a `wall_height_assumed: true` flag.

Wire the enriched assembly output into the Excel export (`build_sheet_takeoff` → the assemblies tab); run gauntlet to confirm room counts are unchanged, then do an end-to-end: upload a CT Pros sheet, classify, export XLSX, open the assemblies tab.

prep.what: Write one integration test that uses the real Docker runner (not a mock) to prove `refreshRepo` completes end-to-end against an already-onboarded repo.

tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
tasks.notes: No durable queue today. This is the production foundation the sweeper (t21) will run on.

prep.what: Build the PG-backed durable job queue: lease rows with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, heartbeat to keep them alive, reclaim stalled jobs, enforce a worker concurrency cap, and schedule jobs only inside the 5h active window.
prep.understand: The sweeper daemon needs a durable queue that survives crashes and prevents duplicate runs. `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is the PG pattern for this — each worker atomically claims exactly one row, no external queue service needed. Heartbeat is a periodic `UPDATE SET heartbeat_at = now()` from the worker; the reclaimer looks for rows where `heartbeat_at < now() - interval` and re-queues them. Window-awareness = `scheduled_at` not before 06:00 or after 22:00 America/New_York. Priority = `high`/`normal` enum, workers prefer `high`. Cap = at most N concurrent workers (controlled by a `max_workers` setting).
approach: Design the `job_queue` schema: `(id, slug, payload jsonb, priority, status, scheduled_at, locked_by, locked_at, heartbeat_at, attempt_count, max_attempts, created_at)` — add a PG migration.

Implement `claimJob(workerId)`: `UPDATE ... SET status='running', locked_by=$1, locked_at=now() WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM job_queue WHERE status='pending' AND scheduled_at <= now() ORDER BY priority DESC, id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *`.
Implement `heartbeat(jobId)` (periodic UPDATE) and `reclaimer()` (finds heartbeat_at > 30s stale → re-queues with attempt_count+1, hard-fails if max_attempts exceeded).
Add window-aware `enqueueAt(job)`: if now is outside the window, push `scheduled_at` to next window open (next 06:00 local).
Write idempotency tests: same `(slug, payload_hash)` re-enqueue is a no-op; concurrent workers each claim distinct jobs; reclaimer re-queues exactly stalled rows.
resources: `lib/db/` — PG connection and migration runner (use `db/migrate.ts` pattern already in the project)
`lib/queue/` — create this module fresh
PG docs: `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (advisory locks not needed here)
Existing `todos_platform` PG instance on VPS — use `lib/pg-board-repository.ts` as reference for the connection pattern
The 5h window config in the triage agent (`lib/triage/governor.ts` or similar)

tasks.title: Daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (prereq for live SWEEPER_REPOS)
tasks.notes: The CLI takes a per-repo O_EXCL lockfile (CLI-vs-CLI only). The daemon's in-process lock is invisible to the CLI. Until done: run refresh ONLY while the sweeper is stopped.

prep.what: Make the sweeper daemon acquire the same per-repo O_EXCL lockfile that the CLI refresh command uses, so CLI and daemon can never race on the same repo.
prep.understand: The CLI's refresh uses `fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx')` (O_EXCL — fails if the file exists) to prevent two CLI runs from refreshing the same repo concurrently. The daemon's job runner has an *in-process* mutex — which is completely invisible to the CLI's file lock. If someone runs `refresh <repo>` while the daemon also has a job for that repo, both proceed and corrupt the worktree. The fix is simple: the daemon must acquire the SAME `lockPath` before starting prep, and release it on job completion or error.
approach: Find the lockfile path in the CLI's refresh code (`lib/sweeper/refresh.ts`): it's typically `path.join(SWEEPER_STATE_DIR, slug + '.lock')` — confirm the exact path.

In the daemon's job runner (`lib/sweeper/daemon.ts` or equivalent), wrap the prep phase: `acquireLock(lockPath)` → run prep → `releaseLock(lockPath)`. Use the same O_EXCL open pattern (`fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx')` then `fs.closeSync(fd)` on release).
If the lock is already held (EEXIST), the daemon should NOT fail the job — instead, re-queue it with a short delay (e.g. 30s). Log the event.
Write a test: spawn the CLI refresh process (holding the lock) → attempt a daemon job for the same repo → verify it queues a retry, not a failure.
resources: `lib/sweeper/refresh.ts` — the CLI's per-repo lock path and O_EXCL pattern
`lib/sweeper/daemon.ts` (or the job runner) — where to insert the lock acquire/release
`SWEEPER_STATE_DIR` env var — the lock directory
Node.js `fs.openSync(path, 'wx')` docs — the O_EXCL equivalent in Node

tasks.title: Pin sandbox image by digest (image axis: mutable tags evade freshness)
tasks.notes: depsState() hashes the image REFERENCE STRING but SWEEPER_REPOS examples use mutable tags (todos-sandbox:laravel). Same-tag rebuild evades freshness detection. Fix: resolve Docker image ID in both refreshRepo and refreshAndCheckBase.

prep.what: Fix `depsState()` so it hashes the Docker image's content-addressable ID (from `docker inspect`) instead of the tag string, catching same-tag rebuilds.
prep.understand: `depsState()` currently does `hash(image_reference_string)`. If `todos-sandbox:laravel` is rebuilt (new toolchain, new packages), the reference string is identical — the hash doesn't change — and the stale image goes undetected. `docker inspect <image> --format={{.Id}}` returns the actual content hash of the image layers. This is the correct thing to hash.
approach: In `lib/sweeper/freshness.ts` (where `depsState()` lives), add `resolveImageId(imageName): string` that runs `docker inspect <imageName> --format={{.Id}}` and returns the sha256 string. Cache it for the duration of the check.
In `depsState()`, replace `hash(image_reference_string)` with `hash(resolveImageId(imageName))`.
Do the same in `refreshRepo` wherever it stores the image hash for same-commit comparison.
Write a minimal test: create two mock `docker inspect` responses with the same tag but different `.Id` values → `depsState()` returns different hashes.
resources: `lib/sweeper/freshness.ts` — `depsState()` implementation
`lib/sweeper/refreshRepo.ts` — where image hash is also computed
`docker inspect --format={{.Id}}` — returns `sha256:...` content hash
